blocks.html: Chapters 1–4 described data already in hand. Real questions in community medicine go beyond it: will this child respond to treatment, and how likely is it that a positive screening result is a false alarm? Probability is the language for that uncertainty, and every confidence interval and hypothesis test later in the book is written in it. This chapter builds probability from its axioms (§5.1), derives the rules for combining probabilities (§5.2–§5.4), turns them into Bayes’ theorem and the arithmetic of screening tests (§5.5), and ends with random variables and the named distributions that inference uses (§5.6–§5.7).
